first.rationale: The two measured declines are onboarding completion (-4%) and activation (-6%), and onboarding completion plausibly sits upstream of activation, so fixing the funnel entry point is the highest-leverage single slot. memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifting completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (fewer signup fields lifting SMB activation) both point the same direction, which is why I want the archived record for memory_86 verified directly rather than trusted at summary level. I also want memory_91 pulled because in-product activation messaging is the direct competitor for this slot and I want to see whether its week-one engagement lift was a real activation gain or a metric that moves without downstream revenue; if the source record shows durable qualified-revenue impact, I would switch. I am deliberately not choosing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing: memory_73 records exactly this temptation and attaches an explicit non-generalization warning plus a material 30-day retention hit, which directly contradicts the sustainable long-term qualified revenue objective. Chasing a price war would buy acquisition against the stated goal. referral_incentive addresses established customers and does not touch either declining metric; enterprise_sales_assist is well-supported but does not respond to this quarter's self-serve deterioration. Downstream value risk: shortening onboarding and cutting signup fields can strip out qualification and firmographic data, degrading lead quality and enterprise routing (memory_44's demo-request path depends on knowing who the prospect is), so revenue could look flatter in volume but worse in quality. I would instrument qualified-pipeline quality and 30-day retention as guardrails, not just completion rate. Uncertainty preserved: all supporting memories are 15-45 days stale, predate the competitor's entry pricing, and were measured in a different demand environment; the current declines may be competitor-driven mix shift rather than a broken funnel, in which case an onboarding fix will underperform its historical effect size. Standard experiment scale with holdout, not broad rollout, so the stale priors get retested rather than assumed.
